newsitem.title: USA: Judge excuses Oklahoma City bombing juror.
newsitem.headline: Judge excuses Oklahoma City bombing juror.

text.p: A potential juror in the Oklahoma City bombing trial who admitted reading recent stories about a Justice Department report on the FBI crime lab was dismissed Friday, the second juror of the day to be excused.

"Given what you have said, I don't think there is any purpose in talking with you further. I am concerned you violated the court's rules and you'll hear from me about that," Federal Judge Richard Matsch told the woman in a stern tone.
The woman, who was the 90th jury candidate to be questioned, said she thought the odds of her being called were "pretty small."
During the questioning, potential jurors are asked to comment on many subjects, including the death penalty and their exposure to news accounts of the case.

The woman was referring to a Justice Department report issued this week after an 18 month investigation that showed the FBI's crime laboratories provided flawed evidence in some major cases, including the Oklahoma City and World Trade Centre bombing cases.

The woman said she understood that the report showed that the FBI's lab results had been "geared toward the prosecution." The woman was the sixth potential juror to be publicly dismissed and the second one on Friday. She is also the second to be dismissed for violating the court's rule to avoid news about the bombing trial.
